subtitle: "Ten questions to check the complete neural-network workflow."
---

Choose one answer per question. Read the feedback for every option, then revisit the relevant episode if the reason is unclear.

::: {.checkpoint title="1 · Predictions and targets"}
Predictions have shape `(8, 1)` and regression targets have shape `(8,)`. What should you do before subtracting them?

- [x] Make their shapes identical, preserving the sample axis.

  Correct: otherwise broadcasting can produce an 8-by-8 matrix of pairwise differences.
- [ ] Multiply both by the batch size.

  This changes values but does not correct the shape mismatch.
- [ ] Assume subtraction automatically pairs the rows.

  Broadcasting follows shape rules, not the scientific meaning of samples.
:::

::: {.checkpoint title="2 · Backward and step"}
What does `loss.backward()` do?

- [x] Calculate gradients of the loss with respect to tracked parameters.

  Correct: an optimiser step then uses these gradients to update the parameters.
- [ ] Choose the next learning rate from the validation set.

  That is a separate tuning or scheduling decision.
- [ ] Update all weights to the optimum.

  Backward calculates derivatives; it neither updates parameters nor solves the optimisation problem.
:::

::: {.checkpoint title="3 · Gradient storage"}
Why does an ordinary mini-batch loop clear gradients before a new update?

- [x] New gradients otherwise accumulate with previous gradients.

  Correct: accumulation is useful when deliberate, but differs from a fresh gradient per batch.
- [ ] The training data must be deleted after every batch.

  Clearing gradients does not delete the input dataset.
- [ ] Clearing gradients resets the learned weights.

  The weights are retained; gradient storage is cleared.
:::

::: {.checkpoint title="4 · Nonlinearity"}
Two affine layers are stacked without an activation. What kind of function can their composition represent?

- [x] Another affine function.

  Correct: the matrix products and biases can be combined into one affine transformation.
- [ ] Every nonlinear function if enough parameters are added.

  Width alone does not make a composition of affine maps nonlinear.
- [ ] Only a constant function.

  The output can still vary linearly with the input.
:::

::: {.checkpoint title="5 · Binary loss"}
What should be supplied to `BCEWithLogitsLoss` for a single binary target?

- [x] Raw logits and floating-point zero/one targets with matching shapes.

  Correct: the loss includes the probability transformation in a stable calculation.
- [ ] Sigmoid probabilities that have already been rounded to zero or one.

  Hard decisions discard information and violate the raw-logit interface.
- [ ] Integer class indices for a four-class problem and one output.

  A mutually exclusive four-class problem usually needs four logits and CrossEntropyLoss.
:::

::: {.checkpoint title="6 · Batch averages"}
Five batches contain 20 samples each and a final batch contains 3. How should you calculate the epoch mean loss from batch means?

- [x] Weight each batch mean by its number of samples, then divide by 103.

  Correct: every observation receives equal weight.
- [ ] Average all six batch means equally.

  This overweights the final three samples.
- [ ] Keep only the final batch's loss.

  That does not summarise the complete training epoch.
:::

::: {.checkpoint title="7 · Evaluation mode"}
Which pair is appropriate for validation of a network containing dropout?

- [x] `model.eval()` together with `torch.no_grad()`.

  Correct: one changes module behaviour, the other disables gradient tracking.
- [ ] Only `torch.no_grad()`, because it disables dropout.

  No-grad does not change dropout's training behaviour.
- [ ] `model.train()` followed by an optimiser step on the validation loss.

  That fits the validation data and invalidates its held-out role.
:::

::: {.checkpoint title="8 · Early stopping"}
The selected validation checkpoint is from epoch 30, while patience expires at epoch 42. Which model should you retain?

- [x] The independent saved copy of epoch-30 weights.

  Correct: restore the checkpoint selected by the stated validation rule.
- [ ] Epoch 42 because it trained longest.

  That ignores the selection rule and may retain an overfitted model.
- [ ] Whichever of the two scores better on the final test set.

  This would use the test set to choose an epoch.
:::

::: {.checkpoint title="9 · Reproducibility"}
Which statement about a fixed seed is justified?

- [x] It helps repeat a run in the same environment, but does not establish robustness across seeds or environments.

  Correct: save the procedure and software versions, and assess variability separately.
- [ ] It guarantees identical results on every future device and library version.

  Numerical kernels and implementations can change across environments.
- [ ] It makes a single test split an exact estimate of future performance.

  Fixing randomness does not eliminate sampling uncertainty or distribution shift.
:::

::: {.checkpoint title="10 · Choosing the model"}
A network and ridge regression are close on validation RMSE. What is a defensible next step?

- [x] Apply a declared selection rule that considers performance and complexity, then evaluate the fixed procedure once on test data.

  Correct: a simpler model can be preferable, and the test set estimates the chosen procedure.
- [ ] Run many network seeds on the test set and report the best one.

  This selects on test noise and gives an optimistic estimate.
- [ ] Choose the network because more parameters guarantee better generalisation.

  Capacity is not evidence of usefulness on new observations.
:::
